ask._doc_: renamed from `human_input`. Same edge semantics: any executable (agent / branch / flow / loop) can target or be targeted. `max_outgoing: 1` enforces the prior 'one answer → next step' shape. Kind renamed to `control_flow` in the manifest, but the dataflow edge shape is unchanged — ask remains a graph node with the same wiring as agent.

branch._doc_: replaces standalone `router` + `condition` connection rows. Both modes (N-ary `switch`, binary `if-else`) share the same connection rules (any executable can target / be targeted). Min/max outgoing match the prior `router` shape (lenient) — `if-else`'s stricter `min_outgoing=1, max_outgoing=2` is enforced at the strategy / IR layer (`BranchStrategy._build_if_else` raises if no `then` target), not at the connection layer.

flow._doc_: replaces standalone `parallel` and `steps` connection rows. `mode` (`parallel` | `sequential`) is a runtime / config concern, not a connection-semantic one — both modes share the same edge rules (any executable can target / be targeted).

tool._doc_: replaces standalone `tools` + `mcp` + `http` dataflow rows. Tool-source rule: no dataflow edges in either direction. The `source` discriminator (`mcp` | `http` | `function`) is a runtime / config concern, not a connection-semantic one — all 3 sources share the same empty edge rule. (wikipedia / tavily_search / duckduckgo / calculator / arxiv_search) — they were tool_source entries that `extended: 'tool'`; legacy envelopes are rewritten by `_compat.migrate_envelope` to `type: 'tool'` + `preset: '<name>'` on read.

edge_kinds._doc_: Per-edge-kind rule tables. per-edge-kind rule tables. The top-level `rules` block above is the `dataflow` table — it controls control-flow edges between executable nodes. `tool_attachment` is the new kind that lets tool-source nodes (`tool` with `source` discriminator `mcp` | `http` | `function`) hand their definition to an Agent; the resulting wiring is NOT in the workflow topology, only in the agent's `tools=[...]` at runtime / exported code generation. Unknown kinds fall back to `dataflow` rules.  `tool` collapses the prior `tools` + `http` + `mcp` rows.  `tool` via the `preset` discriminator — see the `rules.tool` row above.

agent._doc_: An agent can be the TARGET of a tool_attachment edge (it consumes attached tools). Agents are NOT valid sources of tool_attachment edges.

tool._doc_: replaces standalone `tools` + `http` + `mcp` tool_attachment rows. A `tool` node can be SOURCED into an agent. `max_outgoing=null` lets one tool node be wired into N agents. The `source` discriminator (`mcp` | `http` | `function`) is a runtime concern, not a connection-semantic one — all 3 sources share the same `tool_attachment` rule. via the `preset` discriminator.
